segments.title: Chương 301: 0303
segments.content:
This year's sandstorms aren't as fierce as last year's.

But the situation is still quite severe, with an affected area of 680,000 square kilometers, impacting several provinces and cities in the north.

Yang Shuo drove the car over and parked it by the side of the road. Chen Guiliang quickly pulled open the door and got in.

Many pedestrians were well-prepared, carrying masks with them in the spring, ready to put them on as soon as a sandstorm hit.

But some were caught off guard, and could only lift their jackets to cover their mouths and noses.

The source of the sandstorms is the dry salt lakes on the grasslands, which must all be planted with pioneer plants. Currently, seepweed is being planted, but even seepweed struggles to survive. It will take another four or five years of persistent effort to see results.

Farmland also needs to be converted back to forests and pastures, and irrigation dams must be dismantled. Otherwise, new dry salt lakes will appear every year.

"This Capital City is great in every way, except for the climate," Yang Shuo said as he drove. "Never mind the sandstorms, the air itself is so dry. I even got nosebleeds my first winter here. It happened several times in a row, scared me into thinking I had leukemia. I rushed to the hospital for a check-up only to find out it was just the dry air."

Chen Guiliang laughed, "You'll get used to it after a year or two. They'll manage it better in the future."

Yang Shuo said, "I think that's a long shot. It'll take at least another twenty years to fix."

Chen Guiliang didn't respond.

Those guys at Pojie Animation are truly brilliant technicians. Hopefully, we can successfully integrate. I estimate some will probably choose to leave midway.

There's no way Chen Guiliang would let them make something like "Love, Death & Robots."

Putting aside whether they could even make it, where would it be broadcast? So much of the content is not suitable for children, it would never pass the censors.

Although "Larva" also has its share of toilet humor, each episode is only two or three minutes long. Deleting a few episodes here and there wouldn't be a big deal. Besides, Chen Guiliang is only providing the creative concept, letting them handle the specific content. The final product would surely be different from the Korean original.

The same goes for "Yao-Chinese Folktales." Chen Guiliang only told them the story of "Nobody." The rest of the stories, he's letting them create themselves, to do whatever they want.

When Chen Guiliang returned to the company, his secretary informed him that Lu Zhihui was waiting for him in the meeting room.

Chen Guiliang walked into the meeting room and saw Lu Zhihui with a grave expression.

"Is there a problem with financial compliance?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Lu Zhihui said, "The Web 2.0 Expo in San Francisco just ended. It was an unprecedented event, with over ten thousand attendees. All the major companies were there, peddling their products, explaining their ideas, and making all sorts of wild claims."

"That's a good thing," Chen Guiliang said.

Lu Zhihui said, "Reporters discovered that in many of the expo's smaller breakout sessions, the main topic of discussion for investors was their exit strategy."

An investor exit is when venture capital firms cash out and leave. This is either by finding someone to take over their shares midway, or by taking the company public.

But at the breakout sessions of the Web 2.0 Expo, a group of investors was discussing how to go public, which indicated that actually going public had become difficult.

Lu Zhihui added, "The company founders who gave presentations, although they were still going on and on about creativity and innovation, were mostly rehashing old ideas. What they talked about last year, and the year before, they just said it all over again this year. It was very disappointing for the attendees."

"And that bastard O'Reilly even said publicly that there's a little bit of a bubble in Web 2.0. That wasn't his real intention, but it was twisted by the reporters. Now the headlines in the American papers are: O'Reilly Claims Web 2.0 Bubble Has Appeared!"

Hearing this, Chen Guiliang couldn't help but curse, "Fuck!"

O'Reilly was the one who came up with the Web 2.0 concept, and now American newspapers were saying he admitted there was a bubble. Whether there was a bubble or not, this would severely undermine investor confidence and make it even harder for Chen Guiliang to get through an IPO.

Chen Guiliang asked, "So we'll have to spin a new story for the roadshow?"

Lu Zhihui said, "Since the end of last year, investment in Web 2.0 has started to cool down. Web 2.0 has told too many stories before, and now no one wants to hear them. They're even sick of these kinds of stories."

The main issue was still that Web 2.0 hadn't found a mature profit model. In recent years, there had been a constant stream of bad news about layoffs, bankruptcies, and teams disbanding.

The more users a site had, the greater the expense for servers and bandwidth.

Chen Guiliang was in a hurry to develop SP services, ringtones, and promote Weibo precisely to make his revenue figures look better.

As for something like Zhihu, once the user base grew, it would be spun off in the future. It would operate independently, attract venture capital, and be responsible for its own profits and losses. Otherwise, Bytedance's financials would look even worse.

The fact that so many Web 2.0 companies were going bankrupt or laying off staff was also related to the blind investments made by venture capital firms.

They'd invest based on a single concept, a single story, which completely defied investment logic. Many of the founders were clueless themselves, so how could they possibly build something long-lasting?

Lu Zhihui said, "During the IPO roadshow, if you're going to tell a story, President Chen, try to make it more practical. The Americans have heard too much of that flashy, insubstantial stuff, and they're really fed up with it now."

Chen Guiliang muttered, "Practical... then we can only let the data do the talking. O'Reilly is a lunatic. He's the one who came up with the Web 2.0 concept, and he initiated the Web 2.0 Expo. And he actually admitted there's a Web 2.0 bubble at his own expo."

This is what O'Reilly said during his speech: "Some people say Web 2.0 is a bubble. Is that what you all think?"

The people in the audience were either Web 2.0 professionals, Web 2.0 investors, or reporters looking for a big story.

When they heard O'Reilly's question, everyone was stunned: Dude, you can't just say things like that in this kind of setting!

But O'Reilly thought he was being funny. With a mysterious tone and expression, he delivered a twist: "Maybe there is a little bit (of a bubble). But I think great things will come from this. Things are just getting started."

He was obviously trying to create a dramatic effect with his speech, with the second half being his real message.

But the reporters only heard the first half and didn't care what the second half was about.

Even after Lu Zhihui had left, Chen Guiliang remained seated in the conference room, lost in thought.

After a long while, he returned to his office and called Guo Feng in. "Using the interest tags selected by users on Xiaonei and Hainei, the interest groups they've joined, and the keywords from the journals they write themselves, or from searching and browsing others' journals, is it possible to perform a simple behavioral analysis on them?"

Guo Feng asked, "What's the point of analyzing all that?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Our websites have too few ad slots, but I'm afraid that adding more will create a poor user experience. So, I want to implement targeted advertising. Users in different regions and with different interests will see different ad content."

"The specific ad prices will be a bit lower, but the effectiveness of the ads will be better, and the number of ads that can be served in a given time will increase significantly. And it won't affect the user experience."

Guo Feng said, "That kind of technology was released at the end of 2005. The main tool is Google Analytics. It has most of its core functions open and it's free. It's mainly used by e-commerce."

Chen Guiliang asked, "No SNS websites are using it for advertising?"

Guo Feng thought for a moment, "I don't think so in China."

Nor anywhere else.

But they would be soon!

Because the related technology had only matured recently, primarily serving e-commerce platforms.

By the middle of this year, portal websites like Yahoo would start using it for targeted advertising.

By the end of this year, Facebook would also start using it for targeted advertising.

If Chen Guiliang started now, he would be the first SNS website in the world to implement this advertising model.

Bringing this up as a story during the IPO roadshow was guaranteed to make investors' eyes light up!

Chen Guiliang said, "You assemble a team to work on this. If you don't have enough people, find them immediately. You can even poach programmers from e-commerce platforms with high salaries!"

"Is this related to the listing?" Guo Feng asked.
